- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3-5 days), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; reduce forecast peak by 5-10% and add a slight downward slope.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0 to +0.3), model frequently underestimates upside; increase forecast by 2-5% for next 3-5 days.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early horizon (e.g., 1-3 days ahead) when sentiment is volatile; add 1-3% buffer to short-term forecasts.  
- When sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model often lags; forecast should rise 1-2 days ahead of sentiment shift.  
- If recent history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days of price decline), model tends to ignore it; add a 2-5% upward bias to counteract overcorrection.
